newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling eases on unmatched dollar demand.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling eases on unmatched dollar demand.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling lost ground against the dollar on Tuesday, the last trading day of the year, on unmatched demand, commercial bank dealers said.
They said the market was calm for a year end, with many players trading cautiously. One dealer said: "Demand is at normal levels but supply is not enough."
The Central Bank of Kenya posted a mean shilling average of 55.02 against the dollar from 55.00 on Monday while on the pound it posted a mean shilliing average of 93.05 from 92.93.
Dealers said the market opened at 55.00/10 but by mid-morning was trading at 55.13.
"In fact, the shilling has only been held stable by some small inflows from tea and coffee," another dealer said.
Some dealers said that the shilling's downward trend this week was temporary because they expected activity to pick up once the new year begins.
Overnight rates eased at the money market as money from treasury bill maturities flooded the market. They were quoted at 10-15 percent levels from 18-22 percent levels on Monday.
